Subject: HealthCord - follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention

Hi Emma —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call + a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the PoC and security review: 

1) What you told us: HealthCord will send clinical chat prompts (patient symptom descriptions + clinician notes) into Redwood's hosted inference. Primary concerns are PHI in prompts and any derived outputs/summaries. You indicated a need for US-only residency and a retention window for logs.

2) Clarifying questions for the SOC/security team before we lock the MA/PoC:
   • Which specific data elements do you classify as PII/PHI for this integration (SSN, full name + DOB, MRN, free-text with identifiers)?
   • For prompts: do you require that prompts be transient (never persisted) or stored for a short TTL (e.g., 7/30/90 days) for debugging/quality?
   • For outputs: are generated summaries considered PHI and therefore subject to the same retention/residency constraints?
   • Logging controls: do you require obfuscation/redaction of certain fields at ingestion, or is token-level audit logging acceptable if stored in US-only buckets?
   • Residency: you mentioned "US only" — do you need a specific region (us-east-1) or is any US region acceptable?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can confirm the three bullets above (element types / prompt retention TTL / outputs classification), we will produce a short "data handling matrix" and an initial MA/PoC plan that maps retention and residency options to the PoC configuration.
- We'll also attach our standard SOC2 summary and a sample MA clause for ephemeral prompts.

Attachments I plan to add: sample PoC MA plan, SOC2 summary, and a short data handling matrix.

If it's easier, loop in your security contact and we can run a 30-min session to walk through items.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: HealthCord - follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention

Jordan —

Thanks for the recap and for taking notes. Quick answers from our side (copying Raj + security):

• PII/PHI scope: we classify the following as PHI for this integration: full name, DOB, MRN, SSN, contact info, and any free-text that includes those identifiers (e.g., notes containing "patient John Doe").
• Prompts: we prefer prompts to be ephemeral for production — not persisted beyond 30 days for PoC purposes. For debugging during the PoC we can allow up to 90 days but must be able to purge on request.
• Outputs: generated clinical summaries are considered PHI and must follow the same retention and residency constraints as prompts.
• Logging: we need request/response audit logs for compliance but would accept token-level audit logs if they are stored encrypted, with strict access controls, and retained in region. Prefer redaction at ingestion for SSNs and exact DOBs where feasible.
• Residency: must be US-only; our procurement prefers us-east-1 for consistent network egress but we can accept us-west-2 if you have capacity there.

We also attached a short XLS with the specific SOC2 questions our security team will use (soc2-questions.xlsx). Our security lead (security@healthcord.com) will follow up if they need more artifacts.

For the PoC: please send a short data-handling matrix and an action list for purge requests and key rotation / KMS details.

Best,
Emma Sullivan
Director of Product 
HealthCord
emma.sullivan@healthcord.com

Jordan / Marissa —

Drafted the data-handling matrix and a short response bundle for HealthCord. Key points below (I attached the matrix as a PDF stub in case we want to send it to them):

- Prompts: by default our hosted API keeps request payloads in an encrypted short-term store with a configurable TTL. For PoC we can set TTL=90d (default debug) and offer a PoC config for TTL=30d. For production we support TTL down to 0d (ephemeral) if the customer uses our streaming-only mode + no persistent logging.
- Outputs: generated summaries are treated the same as prompts and inherit the TTL and residency settings for the session. We can tag outputs as PHI and route them to US-only buckets.
- Logging: token-level audit logs are available and encrypted; access is locked to the customer's org and Redwood SRE with MFA. We support field-level redaction rules at ingestion via pre-processing hooks (SSN/DOB regex redaction).
- Residency: we can pin to us-east-1 for hosted customers; if capacity is a concern we propose Dedicated nodes in the region.
- Purge procedure: we have an API endpoint for purge requests tied to the deal_id; purges are executed within 24 hours for PoC and 4 hours for production under SLA.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS can be used for payload-at-rest; key rotation follows our standard 90-day rotation cadence and we can provide rotation logs.

Attached: healthcord_data_matrix.pdf (draft)

I'll tidy up the PoC MA plan language (clauses around TTL, purge SLA, region pinning) and send to Jordan for review before we share externally.

—Ben
